title: Al-Musawwir, the Fashioner
hook: the Fashioner, who shapes every face differently (59:24)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Khaliq: the Creator who measures, plans and brings into being. Your line was made. Which three ordinary things did you call made? Day two hundred forty-three.

Stand in a busy train station for five minutes and just look at faces. Thousands of them. Two eyes, a nose, a mouth, every single time. The same few parts. And yet no two are the same. Even identical twins, their mothers will tell you, aren't really identical. Billions of people alive right now, and more who lived before, and somehow each face is its own. How many ways can two eyes and a mouth be arranged? Apparently, enough. Yesterday we met the Creator who measures and plans. The same verse in al-Hashr names, right after it, the one who gives each thing its shape. Today: Al-Musawwir, the Fashioner.
screen: `A TRAIN STATION FULL OF FACES.` → `THE SAME FEW PARTS.` → `NO TWO ALIKE.`

segments.voice: Pickthall calls al-Musawwir the Fashioner. The root is s-w-r, and it gives the word sura, form, shape, image. Tasawwur, imagining, forming a picture in the mind, is from the same root. So al-Musawwir is the one who gives every created thing its particular form: this face, this leaf, this fingerprint. The Qur'an says in Al 'Imran that He is the one who shapes you in the wombs however He wills. In at-Taghabun: He shaped you, and made your shapes good. And in al-Infitar, a surah from the juz' we just read: He created you, then fashioned you, then proportioned you, and in whatever form He willed, He put you together. In ar-Rum, the differences in people's languages and colors are called among His signs. Not a problem to be fixed. A sign. Because the word for image is from this root, Muslim scholars have long discussed making pictures of living beings. Many, drawing on hadith, discouraged it; others permit some kinds, like photographs. That long conversation is part of why mosques are so often decorated with calligraphy, geometry and vines instead of faces. And then a hadith that turns the whole name around. Muslim records the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saying: Allah does not look at your forms, your suwar, or your wealth. He looks at your hearts and your deeds. The Fashioner made every face, and then chose not to judge by it. Which leaves us a question about how we look at faces.
screen: `S-W-R — FORM, SHAPE, IMAGE.` · `SHAPED IN THE WOMB, SHAPES MADE GOOD.` · `COLORS AND LANGUAGES AS SIGNS.` · `HE LOOKS AT HEARTS, NOT FORMS.` · then, large: `EVERY FACE SHAPED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind three faces. One you love. One you barely know, someone you passed today. One you find hard to look at, for whatever reason. Hold each in turn, for a few breaths. Notice the first judgment that arrives, pretty, tired, old, annoying, and gently set it down. Then look again, and just see a face that was shaped, one of a kind, never made before and never again. End with your own face. Look at it the same way. The bell holds the time.
Al-Musawwir. The Fashioner, who gives every created thing its own form, and every face its own shape. Today's word.
Your line: every face shaped. Today, when you look at a stranger's face, catch the first judgment, set it down, and see a face that was fashioned. Day two hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: Muslims reflect on the variety of human faces, colors and languages as signs of the Fashioner; mosque art, following long scholarly discussion of image-making, usually uses calligraphy, geometry and plant forms rather than figures.

fork.setup: the Fashioner shaped every face. what does the Prophet say Allah looks at?

original.note: Arabic: the Fashioner, who gives each thing its form; from s-w-r, image, shape.

trapdoor: what you thought: God as an artist.
what it means: the one who gives every created thing its own form, and then judges hearts, not faces.
what a scholar hears: s-w-r gives sura and tasawwur; 3:6, 64:3, 82:7–8; Muslim 2564, not your suwar but your hearts; the image-making debate.
